dragon_bridge.name: Dragon Bridge
dragon_bridge.shortDescription: Dragon Bridge spans the Han River and links the city-centre area with the eastern side of Da Nang. Its dragon form makes it a familiar landmark along the riverfront route. In the game, it is Little Dragon's first memory stop; check the official tourism portal before making a real-world visit plan.
dragon_bridge.funFact: Da Nang's tourism portal lists Dragon Bridge as 666 metres long, 37.5 metres wide, with six traffic lanes.
dragon_bridge.visitTip: Fire-and-water-show schedules and traffic arrangements can change, so check the current local notice before travelling.

my_khe_beach.name: My Khe Beach
my_khe_beach.shortDescription: My Khe Beach runs along Da Nang's eastern coast, a few kilometres from the city centre according to the city's tourism portal. Its sandy shore, open setting, and seaside activity make it a useful outdoor stop. In the game, the cleanup quest is a conservation message about keeping the beach clean; it is not operational information for the beach.
my_khe_beach.funFact: Da Nang's tourism portal notes that Forbes called My Khe one of the planet's most attractive beaches.
my_khe_beach.visitTip: Follow weather reports, posted beach warnings, and local lifeguard guidance; enter the water only when conditions are safe.

marble_mountains.name: Marble Mountains
marble_mountains.shortDescription: Marble Mountains is a scenic complex in southeast Da Nang with caves, pagodas, and stone stairways. The city tourism portal describes Thuy Son, Kim Son, two Hoa Son peaks, Tho Son, and Moc Son. The game's Five Elements puzzle draws on the place name as storytelling; it does not replace visitor guidance at the site.
marble_mountains.funFact: The Non Nuoc stone-carving village at the foot of the mountains was recognised as National Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2014.
marble_mountains.visitTip: Wear footwear with good grip, follow site signage, and check official ticket, route, and lift information before setting out.

son_tra_peninsula.name: Son Tra Peninsula
son_tra_peninsula.shortDescription: Son Tra Peninsula is a natural area northeast of Da Nang where forest meets the sea and a diverse ecosystem is protected. The city tourism portal identifies the rare red-shanked douc there, while GreenViet runs a conservation programme for the species in Son Tra. The game's quest asks players to observe traces, never to chase or touch wildlife.
son_tra_peninsula.funFact: Da Nang's tourism portal describes Son Tra as the city's green lung and calls the red-shanked douc the “Queen of Primates”.
son_tra_peninsula.visitTip: Use only currently permitted routes; observe quietly from a distance, never feed animals, and do not litter or disturb their habitat.

han_river_bridge.name: Han River Bridge
han_river_bridge.shortDescription: The Han River Bridge is the first swing bridge in Vietnam designed and built by Vietnamese engineers and workers. Spanning the Han River, it connects Hai Chau District with Son Tra District in Da Nang. In the game, this landmark represents urban architectural pride and civic unity; check local traffic schedules and municipal notices on the official tourism portal before planning your visit.
han_river_bridge.funFact: Da Nang's tourism portal notes that the Han River Bridge is 487.7 metres long, 11.9 metres wide, with a rotating central span.
han_river_bridge.visitTip: Bridge swing schedules are set by municipal authorities; check current local announcements on the official portal before going to watch.

linh_ung_son_tra.name: Linh Ung Pagoda Son Tra
linh_ung_son_tra.shortDescription: Linh Ung Pagoda Son Tra is situated on the Son Tra Peninsula, backed by mountains and overlooking the East Sea. The pagoda complex is famous for its 67-metre statue of the Goddess of Mercy standing on a lotus pedestal. In the game, this stop represents peaceful spiritual heritage; remember to dress respectfully and maintain quiet decorum when visiting the real site.
linh_ung_son_tra.funFact: Da Nang's tourism portal highlights the 67-metre Goddess of Mercy statue at Linh Ung Pagoda as one of the tallest Buddha statues in Vietnam.
linh_ung_son_tra.visitTip: Dress modestly, maintain a peaceful atmosphere, and bring a hat and water when walking around the large pagoda grounds.

cham_museum.name: Cham Museum
cham_museum.shortDescription: The Museum of Cham Sculpture in Da Nang is located at the intersection of 2 Thang 9 and Trung Nu Vuong streets. It holds a major collection of Cham sculpture artifacts, including National Treasures. In the game, this cultural stop invites players to appreciate central Vietnam's rich artistic heritage; verify museum opening hours on the official portal before visiting.
cham_museum.funFact: Construction of the Cham Museum began in 1915, and it preserves many representative Cham Pa sculptures.
cham_museum.visitTip: Follow the gallery sequence organized by archaeological origin to better understand the evolution of Cham sculpture art.

non_nuoc_stone_village.name: Non Nuoc Stone Craft Village
non_nuoc_stone_village.shortDescription: Non Nuoc Stone Craft Village is located at the foot of Marble Mountains in Hoa Hai Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District. Formed around the 17th through early 18th centuries, this traditional craft village is recognized as a National Intangible Cultural Heritage. In the game, this location honors the artisanal skill and cultural heritage of local stone sculptors; respect workshop areas when exploring.
non_nuoc_stone_village.funFact: The Non Nuoc stone craft village at Marble Mountains was officially listed as National Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2014.
non_nuoc_stone_village.visitTip: Inquire about prices before buying handcrafted items, and watch your steps when walking through stone carving workshops.

han_market.name: Han Market
han_market.shortDescription: Han Market sits in the heart of Da Nang, bounded by Tran Phu, Bach Dang, Hung Vuong, and Nguyen Thai Hoc streets. Established in the 1940s, this historic commercial hub is famous for regional specialties, dried seafood, and local handicrafts. In the game, this vibrant market stop reflects the bustling everyday culture of Da Nang's riverside district.
han_market.funFact: Han Market originated in the 1940s and remains a landmark traditional market hub along the Han Riverfront.
han_market.visitTip: Explore the market during morning hours to experience the lively atmosphere, and keep your valuables safe in crowded areas.

ba_na_hills.name: Ba Na Hills
ba_na_hills.shortDescription: Ba Na Hills is located on Chua Mountain, about 25 kilometres southwest of central Da Nang. The highland complex is renowned for mountain scenery, European-inspired architecture, and the iconic Golden Bridge. In the game, this destination highlights Da Nang's mountain landscape and major tourism infrastructure; check official visitor information before travelling.
ba_na_hills.funFact: The Golden Bridge at Ba Na Hills gained global acclaim for its golden ribbon structure held by giant stone hands in the mountain clouds.
ba_na_hills.visitTip: Mountain weather changes quickly and is cooler than the city; pack a light jacket and check cable car tickets beforehand.
